title: Let me sign in instead of bookmarking a private admin link
body:
Owner request. Today a wall is managed through a private link that people must bookmark; if they lose it (new phone, cleared browser, another device) they lose their wall. Simulated users hit this too.

Use the engine's accounts capability (Clerk, see BRIEF.md: `clerkHead`, `currentUser`) so people can sign in and see all their walls from any device. Keep it optional and fast: creating a wall without an account should keep working, and existing private links must keep working. Offer to attach a wall to an account (e.g. right after creating it, or from the manage page).

title: Pro: own colours and font on the widget
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Kudospage Pro (a membership: `pro_monthly` $5/month or `pro_yearly` $48/year) already removes the badge: walls whose store row has `member = 1` (see BRIEF.md; earlier one-time buyers have `pro = 1`) (applied when a buyer opens the manage page). Next Pro feature, included at no extra cost: on Pro walls the owner can pick an accent colour and font for the widget and public wall (stored per wall, new additive migration), with a live preview on the manage page. Free walls keep working exactly as today. Tests with `x-test-paid: pro_monthly` (and `x-dw-visitor`).

title: Offer Pro at the moment it is useful (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only think about the badge once they see their widget on their own site. On the manage page next to the embed code, and on the public wall preview, add one calm, dismissible line: 'Want it without the Kudospage badge and in your colours? Pro is $5 per month (or $48 per year), no subscription.' linking to /pricing (or opening checkout directly). No pop-ups, no countdowns, no nagging after it's dismissed. Measure with dw.track.

title: Pro feature: matching cover letter builder
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. The first thing Pro delivers: a cover letter editor that reuses the resume's name, contact details and chosen template so both documents match, with a live A4 preview and PDF download (same print/save path as the resume). Drafts live in the browser like resumes and must never overwrite a resume draft. Non-buyers can open it and see an example, and are offered Pro ($9 once) to write and download their own; buyers (`dwPay.has('pro_pass')` / `paidSkus(c)`) get it fully. Link it from the builder after a resume download ('Need a matching cover letter?'). The resume builder and its free PDF download must not change. The pricing page already shows Pro with its price as 'coming soon' (no buy button) plus refund/terms pages for Paddle; once this feature works, switch that card to a real buy button: `payScript(c)` in the head when `payReady(c)`, a click handler calling `dwPay.open(sku, {next})`, an 'Already bought? Unlock it' link to `/_dw/pay/restore`, and the waitlist form only while checkout is not live (see Kudospage's /pricing for the pattern).

title: Pro feature: Word (.docx) export and several saved versions
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Recruiters and job portals often ask for Word files. For Pro buyers add 'Download Word (.docx)' that produces a clean, editable document of exactly what is on screen (text, line breaks, bullets, non-Latin characters survive), built in the browser. Also let buyers keep several named resume versions (e.g. one per job) in the browser and switch between them without ever losing one. Non-buyers see these options with the price and a short explanation, never a broken button. Free PDF download stays exactly as it is.

title: Pro feature: editable QR codes (subscription, codes keep redirecting after cancel)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. What Pro buyers get: create a code whose short link (e.g. https://qrsthatlast.com/r/<id>, `/r/` is already passthrough in species.json) redirects to a destination they can change any time from a private manage link (and from any browser where they've unlocked Pro). Store codes in D1 (new migration). Show a simple scan count per code. Pro is a subscription (offers pro_monthly $4/month and pro_yearly $36/year in species.json; show both with their billing period). Editing needs an active Pro entitlement (paidSkus has pro_monthly or pro_yearly). When a subscription ends, the code KEEPS redirecting to its last destination; only editing locks, with a plain note and the price to resume. Never redirect a code to a payment or upsell page. The pricing and terms pages already state this promise (price locked while subscribed; 12 months' notice if we ever close); keep them true. Safety (quishing): only http/https destinations, refuse obviously deceptive destinations (IP-address hosts, punycode lookalikes of big brands, URL shorteners chains), rate-limit edits, and add a 'Report this code' link on an interstitial-free abuse page. Non-buyers see what it does and the price. Static codes stay free and unchanged. The pricing page already shows Pro with its price as 'coming soon' (no buy button) plus refund/terms pages for Paddle; once this feature works, switch that card to a real buy button: `payScript(c)` in the head when `payReady(c)`, a click handler calling `dwPay.open(sku, {next})`, an 'Already bought? Unlock it' link to `/_dw/pay/restore`, and the waitlist form only while checkout is not live (see Kudospage's /pricing for the pattern).

title: Mention editable codes when people need them (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only realise they want an editable code when they're about to print. After a download of a Link code, show one calm line under the download buttons: 'Printing this? If the link might change, an editable code lets you update it later without reprinting. $19 once, never expires.' linking to Pro. Dismissible, no pop-ups or pressure, never on Wi-Fi/contact codes. Measure with dw.track.

title: "Will this QR code stop working?" checker
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Build /qr-code-checker: a visitor uploads a picture of any QR code or scans it with the camera, decoded entirely in the browser (nothing uploaded). Show what the code contains and a plain verdict: STATIC (the destination is inside the code itself, nobody can switch it off) or REDIRECT (it points to a short-link/QR service that forwards to the real page; whoever runs that service can change or stop it, and with some providers it stops when a trial or subscription ends). Detect redirects with a maintained list of known QR/short-link service domains plus a generic heuristic (short path on a domain different from the final site); say 'redirects through <domain>', never accuse a company. Then offer: 'Make a permanent static code for the same destination' prefilled in our generator. Also add a short answer page /why-did-my-qr-code-stop-working explaining the cause and the options (ask the provider, reprint with a static code, cover with a sticker), linking to the checker. Works on phones (390 px), camera permission explained before asking. Facts about other products (prices, limits, what is free) must be checked on their own public pages with web search at build time, stated with the date checked, linked to the source, and neutral in tone: no 'scam', no claims we cannot back up (CHARTER law 6). Say plainly that the page is written by the makers of our product. Add the page to the sitemap and link it from the footer or a hub page.

title: More QR types people search for (rendered locally)
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Add generators with their own landing pages for: WhatsApp chat, vCard/contact card, calendar event, geo location, and app-store link. Personal data (names, numbers, addresses) must be rendered in the browser and never put in request URLs. Each page answers the search in its first lines (what it does, that it is free and never expires) and has the working generator at the top.

title: Honest comparison pages: Kudospage vs Senja, Testimonial.to, Famewall
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Build /senja-alternative, /testimonial-to-alternative, /famewall-alternative and a hub /compare. Each page: first lines answer 'what is a cheaper/free alternative to X' with concrete facts; a dated table of what each plan costs over 1 and 3 years next to Kudospage (free forever, Pro $5 per month (or $48 per year)); an honest 'when X is the better choice' section (e.g. video testimonials, integrations we don't have); a clear start button. Also /best-testimonial-tools: a fair roundup of 6-8 real tools including ours with who each is best for (we may list ours first, labelled as ours). Facts about other products (prices, limits, what is free) must be checked on their own public pages with web search at build time, stated with the date checked, linked to the source, and neutral in tone: no 'scam', no claims we cannot back up (CHARTER law 6). Say plainly that the page is written by the makers of our product. Add the page to the sitemap and link it from the footer or a hub page.

title: Import testimonials from a CSV (move from another tool in a minute)
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. On the manage page let the owner upload or paste a CSV exported from another testimonial tool (or any spreadsheet): map columns for text, name, role/company, rating and date with a preview, skip duplicates, mark them as added by the owner (existing source field), never overwrite existing testimonials, and report how many were imported. Mention it on the comparison pages ('bring your testimonials with you').

title: Help for people stuck at a resume-download paywall
body: Owner request, HIGH PRIORITY (growth): we need real visitors. Build (1) /import: paste resume text or drop a PDF/TXT/DOCX the visitor already has; parse it in the browser into our editor fields (name, contact, summary, experience, education, skills) with a review step, never overwriting a saved draft without asking; then free PDF download as usual. (2) Guides /how-to-cancel-resume-io, /how-to-cancel-zety, /how-to-cancel-resume-genius: the real, current cancellation and refund steps taken from each company's own help pages (with links and the date checked), a short polite cancellation/refund email template the visitor can copy, and a link to /import. Not legal advice; factual and calm. Facts about other products (prices, limits, what is free) must be checked on their own public pages with web search at build time, stated with the date checked, linked to the source, and neutral in tone: no 'scam', no claims we cannot back up (CHARTER law 6). Say plainly that the page is written by the makers of our product. Add the page to the sitemap and link it from the footer or a hub page.

title: Download your wall as a self-hosted page (no badge for Pro)
body: Agreed with the owner: our pricing promise says that if Kudospage ever closes, Pro owners get a copy of their wall they can host themselves without the badge. Build that now so the promise is real, and offer it as a feature: on the manage page, 'Download your wall' gives a single self-contained .html file (approved testimonials, the wall's styling, no external requests, no Kudospage script) that can be uploaded to any website or opened offline. Free walls include the small 'Made with Kudospage' link in the file; Pro walls don't. Keep it honest in the copy: the downloaded page is a snapshot and doesn't update itself; the live widget does. Test that the file has no external URLs except the optional attribution link, escapes testimonial text, and matches the approved set at download time.

title: QR design studio: colours, shapes, logo and a 'Scan me' frame
body:
Gap vs QR TIGER, QR Code Generator PRO, Uniqode and QRCode Monkey: every major competitor lets people style the code and we offer almost nothing.

Build a design panel next to the live preview:
- foreground/background colour (plus optional gradient), with a contrast warning when the code would be hard to scan
- dot shape (square, rounded, dots) and corner-eye shape/colour
- upload a logo for the centre (kept in the browser, error correction raised automatically)
- frames with call-to-action text ("Scan me", "Menu", "Free WiFi", custom text)
- a handful of ready-made styles to start from
- a live scannability check (decode the rendered code in the browser and show pass/fail)

Everything stays free for static codes. Size: feature (multi-phase).

title: Print-ready downloads: PNG at print sizes, SVG, PDF and EPS
body: Competitors offer PNG, SVG, PDF and EPS with size presets. Add a download menu with sizes for common uses (business card, flyer, poster, sticker) at 300 dpi, plus vector SVG/PDF/EPS, all generated locally. Show the recommended minimum print size and quiet zone.

title: Bulk QR codes from a CSV or a pasted list (ZIP download)
body: Bulk creation from CSV is a headline feature of QR Code Generator PRO, Uniqode and QR TIGER. Let people paste a list or upload a CSV (one row per code: content, optional file name and label), apply one design to all, preview, and download a ZIP of PNG/SVG plus a printable sheet. Free for static codes, generated in the browser. Good landing page: "bulk qr code generator".

title: Save designs and a brand kit for reuse
body: Competitors let people save designs and reuse brand colours/logo. Save the current design as a named style (in the browser; synced for members), and apply it to any new code in one click.

title: Scan stats for editable codes: scans by day, country and device
body: Analytics (total and unique scans, location, device, time) is the main reason people pay competitors. For editable (Pro) codes, record scans privately (no cookies, no IP storage) and show a simple dashboard with a CSV export. Honest copy about what is and isn't tracked.

title: Hosted QR pages: menu/PDF, digital business card, list of links
body: Competitors host the page a code points to (PDF menu, vCard page, link-in-bio, app download page). Offer a few hosted page types for editable codes with a clean mobile page, and explain clearly that static vCard/URL codes stay free and never expire.

title: Template gallery: 10+ designed templates with colours, fonts and spacing
body: Gap vs Kickresume (40+ templates), Enhancv, Zety, Resume.io: we offer three. Build a gallery of at least ten distinct, good-looking templates (still ATS-readable: real text, standard headings; any two-column design must be labelled as less ATS-safe), with accent colour, font pair, density and optional photo controls, and live thumbnails rendered from the person's own content. Size: feature or redesign.

title: Import an existing resume (PDF or pasted text, LinkedIn PDF export)
body: Kickresume, Teal and Enhancv let people start from an existing resume or LinkedIn profile. Parse a PDF (in the browser) or pasted text into sections and fields, show what was found for a quick check, and fill the builder. No upload to a server.

title: Tailor to a job: paste a job ad, see matched and missing keywords
body: Keyword matching against a job description is the core of Rezi, Jobscan and Teal. Let people paste a job ad; show a match score, the important skills/keywords that are missing, where to add them, and keep a tailored copy per job. Computed locally, honest about what ATS software really does.

title: Writing help: bullet suggestions per job title and a bullet improver
body: Every competitor has an AI or phrase library for bullets and summaries (Kickresume has 20,000 phrases). Build a large curated library of example bullets and summaries per job title (reuse the examples pages), searchable from each section, plus an improver that flags weak bullets (no action verb, no number, too long, 'responsible for') with concrete rewrites.

title: Real PDF download with 'fit to one page'
body: Download today relies on the browser print dialog. Generate a proper PDF file directly (selectable text, correct margins, file named after the person) with a 'fit to one page' control that adjusts spacing and font size within readable limits, and a page-break preview.

title: Job application tracker
body: Teal and Huntr win high-volume job seekers with a tracker. A simple board (saved, applied, interview, offer) with company, link, date, which resume/cover letter was sent and notes, stored in the browser (synced for members).

title: Widget gallery: masonry, carousel, marquee, single card, rating badge, popup
body: Gap vs Senja (20+ widget templates), Testimonial.to, Famewall: we have one wall look. Build a widget gallery with live preview of the owner's real testimonials: masonry wall, carousel, scrolling marquee, single featured card, compact star-rating badge and a small corner popup; each with light/dark and accent colour, and one copy-paste embed snippet. Size: feature or redesign.

title: Better testimonials: photo, company logo, role, and highlighted phrases
body: Competitor walls look credible because each testimonial shows a face, title, company and a highlighted key phrase. Let customers add a photo and role on the collection form (owner can add a logo), and let the owner highlight a phrase that the widgets emphasise. Store images within the existing storage limits.

title: Collection form builder: questions, star rating, thank-you page, reminder link
body: Senja and Testimonial.to win on collection. Let owners customise the form's prompts/questions, rating, permission checkbox, thank-you message with a CTA, and generate an email/text template plus a one-click reminder link to send customers. Measure completion.

title: Paste-in import from Google, X, LinkedIn, Product Hunt and others
body: Senja imports from 20+ platforms. Without new APIs, let owners paste a review's text and link (or a list) and auto-format it: name, rating, date, source icon and a link to the original, marked as imported.

title: Share a testimonial as an image for social posts
body: Senja and others turn testimonials into shareable images. Render any testimonial as a branded square/story PNG in the browser (a few layouts) for Instagram, LinkedIn and X, with a small 'kudospage' mark on free walls.

title: Google review stars: schema.org markup on the wall page
body: Testimonial.to lists Google rich snippets as a paid feature. Add correct schema.org Review/AggregateRating markup on public wall pages (following Google's self-serving review rules honestly) and explain it on a landing page.
